item.title: Uncovering New Insights into Green Space Accessibility with Mobile Location Data
item.dc:title: Uncovering New Insights into Green Space Accessibility with Mobile Location Data
item.dc:creator: Niall Newsham Somayeh Dodge Karen Seto a Department of Geography, University of California, Santa Barbara, USAb Yale School of the Environment, Yale University, USANIALL NEWSHAM is a Postdoctoral Research Scholar in the Department of Geography, University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA 93106. E-mail: nnewsh@ucsb.edu. His research interests include human–nature interactions, population change dynamics, and the spatiotemporal dimensions of population decline.SOMAYEH DODGE is an Associate Professor of Spatial Data Science in the Department of Geography, University of California, Santa Barbara, Santa Barbara, CA 93106. E-mail: sdodge@ucsb.edu. Her research develops spatiotemporal data analytics, machine learning, modeling, and visualization techniques to study movement in human and ecological systems.KAREN SETO is the Frederick C. Hixon Professor of Geography and Urbanization Science at the Yale School of the Environment, Yale University, New Haven, CT 06520. E-mail: karen.seto@yale.edu. Her research integrates remote sensing, field interviews, and modeling methods to study urbanization and its consequences, the drivers of urban expansion, and forecasting urban expansion.

item.dc:title: Historical Long-Term Ultra-Fine-Scale Analysis of Urban Landscape Change with KH-9 PCS Images
item.dc:creator: Amir Reza Shahtahmassebi Golnaz Shahtahmassebi Nathan Moore Peter M. Atkinson a Architectural Engineering School, Qingdao Hengxing University of Science and Technology, Chinab Department of Physics and Mathematics, School of Science and Technology, Nottingham Trent University, UKc Department of Geography, Environment, and Spatial Sciences, Michigan State University, USAd Lancaster Environment Centre, Lancaster University, UKAMIR REZA SHAHTAHMASSEBI is an Associate Professor in the Architectural Engineering School at Qingdao Hengxing University of Science and Technology, Qingdao, 266100, China. E-mail: amirreza208@hotmail.com. His research interests include remote sensing, GIScience, pattern recognition, historical landscape mapping, deep learning, and urban growth.GOLANZ SHAHTAHMASSEBI is an Associate Professor in the School of Science and Technology at Nottingham Trent University, Nottingham, NG1 4FQ, UK. E-mail: golnaz.shahtahmassebi@ntu.ac.uk. Her research interests include dynamic models and their applications in real life, statistical learning theory, Bayesian inference, computational statistics, sequential Monte Carlo methods and particle filters, statistical image processing, and specializing in applied statistics—the foundation of modern machine learning and artificial intelligence.NATHAN MOORE is an Associate Professor in the Department of Geography at Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48823. E-mail: moorena@msu.edu. His research interests include modeling climate and land-use interactions in the developing world, remote sensing of land-use change, and the technosphere.PETER M. ATKINSON is a Distinguished Professor in the Lancaster Environment Center at Lancaster University, Bailrigg, Lancaster LA1 4YW, UK. E-mail: pma@lancaster.ac.uk. His research interests include machine learning, artificial intelligence and Earth observation, with a methodological focus on scale, change-of-support theory and image fusion, and a wide range of science areas from ecology, through natural hazards, to spatial epidemiology.
